extracted.intended_audience: national IP offices, industrial property officials, IP attorneys, layout-design creators and rights-holders, and policymakers in Member States party to the Bangui Agreement
extracted.subtask_description: Legal and procedural standards for protection, registration, enforcement, licensing, and exceptions for layout designs (topographies) of integrated circuits, together with related unfair-competition standards. Covers eligibility, originality, filing and publication formalities, opposition and appeal procedures, licensing (voluntary and non-voluntary), and remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: General standard of unfair competition (honest practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apart from the acts and practices referred to in Articles 2 to 6, an act of unfair competition shall be any act or practice which, in the course of industrial or commercial activities, is contrary to honest practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to acts/omissions in industrial, commercial or liberal-profession activities; triggers civil remedies (injunctions, damages, other civil remedies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies for unfair competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Any natural or legal person who has suffered damage or is liable to suffer damage due to an act of unfair competition may institute proceedings before the court of a Member State and may obtain injunctions, damages and any other remedy provided by civil law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts may award injunctions and damages and use other civil-law remedies available under domestic law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfair competition applies independently of IP protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles 1 to 6 shall apply independently of and in addition to any legislative provision protecting inventions, industrial designs, trademarks, literary and artistic works and other subject matter of intellectual property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unfair-competition claims are available even where other IP rights exist; they are cumulative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confusion with another's enterprise or activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Any act or practice which, in the course of industrial or commercial activities, generates or is likely to generate confusion with the enterprise or activities of another person, in particular with the products or services proposed by such enterprise, shall constitute an act of unfair competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers both actual and likely confusion; remedies available where confusion concerns identity of source or business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms of confusion (non-exhaustive list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Confusion may concern, in particular: a trademark (registered or not), a trade name, a distinctive sign of an enterprise other than a trademark or trade name, the external appearance of a product, the get-up of products or services, and a famous person or well-known fictional character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This list illustrates typical elements whose use may create confusion; includes non-trademark signs and product appearance/get-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts damaging to another's image or reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: Any act or practice which, in the course of industrial or commercial activities, damages or is liable to damage the image or reputation of another’s enterprise, whether the act or the practice generates confusion or not, shall constitute an act of unfair competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Liability does not depend on confusion; focus is on damage or likelihood of damage to reputation or image.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms of damage to image or reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: Damage to another’s image or reputation may result, in particular, from a weakening of the image or reputation attaching to: a trademark, a trade name, the distinctive sign of an enterprise other than a trademark or trade name, the external appearance of a product, the get-up of products or services, and a famous person or well-known fictional character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes weakening of distinctive character or advertising value; 'weakening of the image or reputation' is defined as lessening distinctiveness or advertising value of marks, get-up, product appearance, or famous persons/characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misleading the public
rubrics_metrics.description: Any act or practice which, in the course of industrial or commercial activities, misleads or is likely to mislead the public with respect to an enterprise or its activities, in particular the products or services proposed by the enterprise, shall constitute an act of unfair competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers both actual misleading and likely misleading; emphasis on public perception regarding enterprise, products or services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific elements that may mislead the public
rubrics_metrics.description: The public may be misled by advertising or promotional activities, particularly with respect to: the manufacturing process of a product; the suitability of a product or service for a given purpose; the quality, quantity or other characteristic of a product or service; the geographical origin of a product or service; the conditions under which a product or service is proposed or supplied; and the price of a product or service or its method of calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates typical factual claims that, if false or misleading, can constitute unfair competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disparaging another's enterprise or activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Any false or abusive allegation, in the course of industrial or commercial activities, which discredits or is liable to discredit another’s enterprise or activities, in particular the products or services proposed by the enterprise, shall constitute an act of unfair competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on false/abusive claims intended to discredit; overlaps with misleading/public-damage concepts but centers on disparagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of disparagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Disparagement may result from advertising or promotional activities and concern, in particular, the manufacturing process, suitability for purpose, quality/quantity/characteristics, geographical origin, supply conditions, and price or method of calculation of a product or service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same illustrative categories as for misleading the public; demonstrates how advertising can be the vehicle for disparagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfair competition concerning confidential information
rubrics_metrics.description: Any act or practice which, in the course of industrial or commercial activities, leads to the disclosure, acquisition or use by third parties of confidential information without the consent of the person legally entitled to possess such information, in a manner contrary to honest commercial practice, shall constitute an act of unfair competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers disclosure, acquisition and use; central standard is absence of consent and conduct contrary to honest commercial practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts constituting improper disclosure/acquisition/use of confidential information
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure, acquisition or use of confidential information by a third party without the consent of the lawful holder may, in particular, result from: industrial or commercial espionage; breach of contract; breach of trust; instigation to commit such acts; and acquisition by a third party who knew the acquisition involved such acts or whose ignorance constituted gross negligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates typical wrongful means of acquiring confidential information; knowledge or gross negligence suffices for liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of confidential information (three-part test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information shall be considered 'confidential' when: (a) in its totality or configuration it is not generally known to persons who normally deal with that type of information or is not readily available to them; (b) it has commercial value because it is confidential; and (c) its lawful holder has taken reasonable precautions, in view of the circumstances, to keep it confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets thresholds for protection: novelty to relevant circles, commercial value derived from confidentiality, and reasonable protective measures by the holder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dishonest use or disclosure of regulatory/confidential test data
rubrics_metrics.description: Any act which constitutes dishonest use in commerce of confidential data obtained from tests or other confidential data whose production requires considerable effort and which have been communicated to a competent authority for obtaining authorization to market pharmaceutical or agricultural chemical products comprising new chemical entities, or disclosure of such data (save where necessary to protect the public or unless measures ensure protection), shall be considered an act of unfair competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special protection for regulatory test data; disclosure/use is permitted only where necessary to protect public health or effective safeguards exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disorganization of a competing enterprise and market
rubrics_metrics.description: Any act or practice which, in the course of industrial or commercial activities, is liable to disorganize a competing enterprise, its market or the market of the profession concerned, shall constitute an act of unfair competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets conduct that undermines a competitor's operations or a market's functioning; may be actionable even absent direct deception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Means by which disorganization may be achieved
rubrics_metrics.description: Disorganization may be achieved by: suppression of advertising; diverting of orders; practicing abnormally low prices; disorganizing the sales network; poaching staff; inducing staff to strike; and failure to comply with regulations governing exercise of the activity concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides concrete examples of competitive conduct that can amount to unfair competition via market/enterprise disorganization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of damages for unfair competition
rubrics_metrics.description: The competent domestic court shall take into consideration the negative economic consequences, including loss of profits, suffered by the injured party, the profits made by the author of the wrongful act and the moral prejudice caused to the victim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts consider both economic loss and wrongful gains, and also moral prejudice; forms the basis for quantifying compensation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: integrated circuit and layout design (topography)
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrated circuit: a product, in final or intermediate form, in which the elements, at least one active, and some or all interconnections are integrally formed in or on a piece of material and intended to perform an electronic function. Layout design (topography): the three-dimensional disposition of the elements and interconnections of an integrated circuit, or such disposition prepared for an integrated circuit intended for manufacture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the subject matter of protection and the technical concept to which the Annex applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter and protection eligibility (commercial exploitation limit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Layout designs of integrated circuits may be protected under this Annex if, and to the extent that, they are original. A registration may be applied for only if the layout design has not yet been commercially exploited or has been commercially exploited for not more than two years anywhere in the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-part eligibility: originality plus the filing/exploitation time-bar (≤2 years commercial exploitation globally).

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality requirement for layout designs
rubrics_metrics.description: A layout design shall be deemed original if it is the result of its creator’s own intellectual effort and is not commonplace among creators of layout designs and manufacturers of integrated circuits. A layout design that consists of a combination of elements and interconnections that are commonplace shall be protected only if the combination, taken as a whole, is original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originality is judged against commonality among practitioners; combinations of commonplace elements can be protected if the overall combination shows original intellectual effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to protection and ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to protection of a layout design shall belong to its creator. It may be assigned or transferred by succession. Where several persons have jointly created a layout design, the right shall belong to them jointly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default ownership rules: creator(s) own the right unless contract or succession provides otherwise; supports transfers and joint ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint ownership of certificates — exploitation and licensing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Joint owners: each joint owner may exploit the creation for his own benefit subject to equitable compensation for other joint owners who do not exploit; each joint owner may take action for infringement for his own exclusive benefit (notify other joint owners; judgment deferred until notification proven); each may grant non-exclusive licenses for own benefit subject to equitable compensation and notification (others may oppose by acquiring share); exclusive licenses require agreement of all joint owners or court authorization; assignment rules include right of first refusal for other joint owners for three months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed procedural rules govern exploitation, enforcement, licensing, transfer and relinquishment among joint owners; compensation and notification requirements apply; failure to agree triggers court-set pricing and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to designs created under contract or employment
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a layout design has been created under a contract for service or an employment contract, the right to protection shall belong to the commissioner or to the employer, unless otherwise provided in the contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracts/employment agreements can assign ownership to commissioner/employer by default unless contract states otherwise—importance of explicit contractual terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights conferred — unlawful acts without authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to Articles 8 and 20, the following acts shall be unlawful when carried out without the authorization of the holder: (a) reproducing, whether by incorporation in an integrated circuit or otherwise, a protected layout design in its entirety or any part thereof, except reproducing any part that does not fulfill the requirement of originality; and (b) importing, selling or otherwise distributing for commercial purposes a protected layout design, an integrated circuit in which a protected layout design is incorporated or an article in which such integrated circuit is incorporated to the extent it continues to contain a layout design unlawfully reproduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protection applies both to reproduction and commercial distribution/importation of unlawfully reproduced designs; exceptions and limitations in Article 8 narrow the scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations/exceptions to rights conferred
rubrics_metrics.description: The protection shall not extend to: (a) reproduction of a protected layout design for private purposes or for the sole purpose of evaluation, analysis, research or teaching; (b) incorporation in an integrated circuit of a layout design based on such analysis or evaluation and itself possessing originality; (c) acts referred to in Article 7(b) where done with respect to a design placed on the market by the holder or with his consent; (d) acts where the person performing or ordering the act did not know and had no reasonable grounds to know, when acquiring the integrated circuit or article, that it incorporated an unlawfully reproduced layout design (subject to notice and limitation to stocks already acquired and reasonable royalty once advised); and (e) acts with respect to an identical original layout design created independently by a third party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates fair-use/research exceptions, exhaustion/consent (marketed by holder), bona fide purchasers, independent creation, and conditions for post-notification compensation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start and term of protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Protection takes effect either (a) on the date of the first commercial exploitation of the layout design anywhere in the world by the holder or with his consent, provided an application for protection is filed within the time limit referred to in Article 2(2); or (b) on the filing date allocated to the application if the layout design has not been the subject of prior commercial exploitation. The protection ceases at the end of the tenth calendar year following the date on which it took effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two possible triggers for the start date depending on prior exploitation; fixed maximum term of ten calendar years from effect date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing an application — one application per layout design
rubrics_metrics.description: A separate application shall be filed for each layout design. An application shall be filed with the Organization or national service responsible for industrial property, following procedures in implementing regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative requirement: one design per application; comply with both Agreement and implementing regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application contents — mandatory documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The file shall contain: (a) an application for registration addressed to the Director-General bearing applicant’s name, address, nationality and habitual residence where different; (b) document proving payment of required fees; (c) a short and precise description of the layout design with sufficient information on how best to exploit it known to the creator on the date of deposit and priority date if claimed; (d) powers of applicant’s agent where appropriate, a copy or drawing of the layout design together with information defining the electronic function intended; applicant may omit manufacturing-method parts if submitted parts suffice for identification; (e) date of first commercial exploitation anywhere in world or statement exploitation not begun; and (f) particulars establishing entitlement to protection under Article 4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both formal and technical information required; applicant may omit manufacturing method detail provided identification is still possible; proof of fee payment is mandatory (see Article 11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadmissibility for non-payment of fees
rubrics_metrics.description: No application for registration shall be acceptable if it is not accompanied by a document attesting payment of the required fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment proof is a threshold formality; absence leads to inadmissibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date allocation — admissibility conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization shall allocate as the filing date the date of receipt of the application, written in one of its working languages, by the Ministry responsible for industrial property or by the Organization, provided that, at the time of receipt, the application contains: (a) an express or implicit indication that registration is requested; (b) information whereby the identity of the applicant may be established; (c) a copy or drawing of the layout design; and (d) proof of payment of the prescribed fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing date depends on minimal content at receipt; missing any of the four elements prevents allocation of filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing of applications — required publication details
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization shall publish for each registered layout design: the application number; the title of the layout design; the filing date and where applicable the date of first exploitation; the name and address of the applicant; the name and address of the agent, if any; the name and address of the author(s) unless request excluded; and the descriptions and representations, if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication provides transparency; applicants may request exclusion of author names when publishing the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to registration — grounds and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Any interested party may oppose the registration by sending to the Organization, within three months from the publication mentioned in Article 13, a written statement setting out the reasons for opposition, which reasons must be based on an infringement either of the provisions of Articles 1, 2 or 3 of this Annex, or of a prior registered right belonging to the opposing party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposition window is three months from publication; grounds are limited to defined statutory grounds (definitions/confusion/originality) or prior registered rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition procedure and replies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization shall send a copy of the statement of opposition to the applicant or agent, who may reply within a once-renewable period of three months; reply forwarded to opponent. Before deciding the Organization may hear parties on request. Decision is appealable to High Commission of Appeal within 60 days from receipt of notice. Registration declared forfeit if opposition valid; final cancellation decision published in special register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timelines: opponent files within 3 months; applicant replies within up to 6 months if renewal; appeal period 60 days; publication of final decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim of ownership before the Organization — procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: When a person not entitled to registration files an application, the person entitled may claim ownership before the Organization within three months from publication. The Organization sends copy of claim to applicant who may reply within a once-renewable period of three months. Parties may be heard on request. Organization decision appealable to High Commission of Appeal within 60 days. If claim valid, Organization transfers application to claimant and publishes final decision in the special register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parallels opposition procedure; focuses on rightful ownership claims with similar timelines and appeal rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of applications limited to formal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization shall examine each application to determine whether it complies with the requirements of Articles 2 and 10 above, without carrying out an examination of originality, of the applicant’s right to protection or of the correctness of the statements made in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No substantive examination of originality or entitlement—Organization performs formal/admissibility check only; substantive disputes handled via opposition, claim, or court actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions governing rejection and correction periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application does not comply with Article 10 (except fee proof) it shall be returned to applicant to correct within three months (extendable by 30 days for justifiable need). Corrected application retains initial date. If not corrected within period, application rejected. Rejection pronounced by Director-General; applicant must be given opportunity to correct before rejection. Organization may automatically correct obvious clerical errors. Applicant may appeal rejection within 60 days from notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correction window generally 3 months + possible 30-day extension; automatic clerical corrections allowed; appeal rights to High Commission within 60 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration of applications and publication of registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Organization ascertains that an application complies with Articles 2 and 10, it shall register the layout design in the special register by decision of the Director-General or authorized official. Prior to registration, any application may be withdrawn. For each registered layout design the Organization shall publish entries including registration number, title, filing date and date of first commercial exploitation (if stated), holder name/address, agent, author names (unless excluded), and descriptions and representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration is administrative decision; publication follows registration; applicants may withdraw pre-registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special register of layout designs and implementing regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization shall keep a special register of layout designs in which it shall make all entries provided in this Annex. The implementing regulation shall lay down the acts to be registered and published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The register is authoritative for rights against third parties and for public notice; implementing regulations provide further operational detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to information in the special register
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may, at any time, on payment of the prescribed fee, consult the special register of Layout Designs or request, at his own expense, information, extracts or copies of such information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access is available to the public for a fee; supports transparency and due-diligence searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer, assignment and written-form requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Rights subsisting in an application for registration or in a layout design shall be transferable in whole or in part. Acts involving transfer of ownership, licensing the right of exploitation, assignment, pledge or cancellation of a pledge shall, on pain of invalidity, be evidenced in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal writing requirement for validity of transfers/licensing/pledges; supports reliable recording and registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording and publication of transfers and related acts
rubrics_metrics.description: Acts referred to in Article 22 shall not be binding on third parties unless they are entered in the special register of layout designs; a record of such acts shall be kept by the Organization. Subject to regulation conditions, Organization shall furnish copies or certificates of entries on request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration of transfers is necessary for third-party effect; Organization provides certified evidence on request.

rubrics_metrics.name: License contract formalities and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: The holder may, by contract, grant a license enabling a person to exploit the protected layout design. Duration of the license may not be longer than that of the layout design. The license contract shall be entered in the special register; it shall not be binding on third parties unless entered and published in the specified format. License may be cancelled from the register upon proof of expiry or termination. In absence of contrary provisions, grant of a license does not preclude licensor from granting other licenses or exploiting the layout design himself. Grant of an exclusive license precludes the licensor from granting licenses to others and, absent contrary provisions, from exploiting the design himself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key contractual and registration requirements: register entry required for third-party effect; default non-exclusivity unless exclusive license agreed; exclusive license restricts licensor's further exploitation absent contrary terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalid clauses in license contracts (anti-competitive restrictions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clauses in license contracts shall be invalid insofar as they constitute anti-competitive practices and generally impose on the licensee, in the industrial or commercial sphere, restrictions not deriving from the rights conferred by the layout design or not necessary for upholding such rights. The following are not considered restrictions: restrictions relating to extent, scope or duration of exploitation of the layout design; and the obligation on the licensee to refrain from acts liable to impair the validity of the layout design. In absence of provisions to the contrary, the license shall not be assignable and the licensee shall not be authorized to grant sublicenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance between lawful licensing controls and competition law; courts recognize invalid clauses at request of interested party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-voluntary (compulsory) license for non-working — grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: At the request of any person made four years from the filing date of the application, or three years from the date of registration (whichever later), a non-voluntary license may be granted where one or more conditions are fulfilled: (a) protected layout design is not being worked on the territory of a Member State at the time the request is made; (b) working does not meet the demand for the protected product on reasonable terms; or (c) refusal of the holder to grant licenses on reasonable commercial terms unfairly and substantially prejudices establishment or development of industrial or commercial activities on such territory. Notwithstanding, a non-voluntary license may not be granted if the holder provides legitimate reasons for the non-working.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compulsory license mechanisms are time- and fact-limited; courts will balance public/market needs against holder's legitimate reasons for non-working.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for non-voluntary license — forum and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Request shall be made to the civil court of the domicile of the holder or, if holder domiciled abroad, to civil court of elected domicile or place where holder named an agent for filing. Only requests by persons domiciled in a Member State considered. The request shall contain: name and address of requester; title and number of layout design; in case under Article 27, a statement undertaking to work the layout design on territory to meet market needs. The request shall be accompanied by proof the requester previously approached the holder by registered letter requesting contractual license on reasonable commercial terms and proof the requester is capable of working the protected layout design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict procedural and evidentiary prerequisites: domicile rule, prior unsuccessful negotiation via registered letter, capability to exploit, and undertaking to work the design locally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant of non-voluntary license — court procedure and decision content
rubrics_metrics.description: Civil court examines whether request satisfies requirements; if not, rejects after allowing corrections. If requirements met, court notifies holder and any licensee in register and invites observations in writing within three months, holds hearing and then decides to grant or refuse. If granted, decision shall specify the scope of the license (acts covered per Article 7(b) and period; note that a non-voluntary license under Article 27 cannot extend to importation) and the amount of remuneration to be paid by the licensee to the holder; in absence of agreement, remuneration shall be equitable and subject to judicial revision. Decision must be in writing, state grounds, be conveyed to the Organization which shall register and publish it and notify parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court-specified scope and equitable remuneration; notification/publication ensures enforceability and transparency; remedy includes judicial revision of remuneration.
